conventions.convention: The ambient real field is Dedekind complete. Coordinates and optional weights are exact dyadic rationals; absent weights mean zero. Inputs are nonempty finite lists with distinct integer stable identifiers.

Unweighted duplicates are equal coordinates; weighted duplicates are equal coordinate-weight pairs. Each duplicate class retains its least identifier; unequal weights at equal coordinates remain distinct.

Orientation rows are (p,1), and lifted rows are (p, squared norm minus weight,1). The power determinant satisfies P = −OΔ; the normalized product OP is positive inside, zero on, and negative outside the power sphere.
Ranks start at zero in one fixed universe containing auxiliary sites. Height perturbations are positive formal monomials ε^(2^rank), ordered by the least nonzero exponent; no numerical ε is chosen.

Voronoi cells are closed and contain every distance tie. Weak empty-circle conditions exclude strictly interior sites but permit cocircular sites. Hull boundary counts include sites subdividing straight hull edges.
Nearest-site ties use the least stable identifier; a minimizing site is returned even outside the convex hull. Hull boundary queries count as inside.

The randomized history algorithm requires both input and augmented general position and one uniformly random insertion permutation. Its complexity counts exact predicate calls, excluding arbitrary-precision bit cost.

The 3D algorithm omits projected dependent four-site bases and records them as degenerate-base. Projected dimension below three returns a dimension and deduplicated list without a tetrahedralization claim.

load_bearing.statement: For projected affine dimension d ∈ {2,3}, lower simplices of the fixed formal lift cover conv(P), intersect in common faces, and have weakly empty power spheres for the original unperturbed weighted sites.
For an affinely independent base and a common power sphere, P_d = −O_dΔ(q) and O_dP_d = −O_d²Δ(q); the normalized sign is positive inside, zero on, and negative outside.

For one fixed finite universe and an affinely independent base, every exact nonzero power determinant retains its sign, every exact zero has a nonzero polynomial tie determinant, and all tuples receive coherent signs without selecting a numerical perturbation.

For every nonempty finite indexed dyadic planar site set, the algorithm terminates after duplicate collapse; its full-dimensional prefix triangulations are the fixed formal lower triangulations, and deleting synthetic-vertex triangles leaves a weak empty-circle triangulation of the input hull. Dimensions zero and one return the prescribed point or chain.

Every finite full-dimensional dyadic planar site set admits a strictly containing dyadic supertriangle whose vertices are strictly outside every circumcircle through a noncollinear input triple; input general position permits augmented general position.
For a strictly convex counterclockwise quadrilateral ABCD, if D lies formally below the plane through A,B,C, changing diagonal AC to BD strictly decreases the defined lifted interpolation integral.
For n distinct planar sites of affine dimension two and k hull-boundary sites, 3T = 2E − k and n − E + T = 1, hence T = 2n − 2 − k and E = 3n − 3 − k.
A full-dimensional convex polytope in R⁴ with m ≥ 5 vertices has at most m(m−3)/2 facets.

concerns.concern: The Definition calls D = {m2^e : m,e ∈ Z} the real field's “dyadic subfield.” This set is a subring, not a subfield: 3 belongs to D but its inverse 1/3 does not. The same incorrect terminology is repeated in F4 of lem-large-delaunay-supertriangle-exists. The explicit coordinate set is clear, and the reviewed arguments perform divisions in the ambient real field, but the terminology should be corrected consistently.

Step 4.1 says: “The normalized determinant therefore has the sign of the difference between the query height and the plane through A,B,C.” With the cited convention, P = −O(h_query−plane), so OP has the opposite sign of that difference. The Statement and Steps 1.1–3.1 use the correct below-plane condition and establish the integral inequality; this sentence reverses the established normalization.

The Definition calls a site hidden when its original lift “is not a vertex of any lower face,” whereas the algorithm's hidden report and the correctness theorem concern the fixed formal lift. These notions can differ. Give ids 1–4 to 0,4e1,4e2,4e3, id 5 to (1,1,1), and every site weight ||p||². All original heights are zero, so the interior site's lift is not an extreme vertex. Its perturbed height ε^16 is strictly below the corner-interpolating height (ε+ε²+ε⁴+ε⁸)/4, so it appears in the formal lower triangulation. The theorem explicitly qualifies its claim as formal; the Definition and algorithm should distinguish original-hidden from formal-hidden to make their interface unambiguous.

seams_checked.note: Checked the determinant definition, generic exact fallback, certified predicate algorithm and soundness theorem, with their supporting arguments. Batch 15 preserves row/column order, raw zero and degenerate-base handling. Its weighted tests use the generic dyadic determinant procedure; its formal height tie rule is separately defined and proved locally.

Read the downstream page and the Delaunay uses in alg-delaunay-seeded-curved-uniform-nvb-refinement and thm-curved-uniform-nvb-quality-and-termination. The consumer supplies four dyadic square corners, permits their cocircular tie through ordinary g=0 insertion, and uses the supplier for hull triangulation and coherent ties. Its right-isosceles seed geometry is derived from the square coordinates; no general Delaunay angle guarantee is attributed to this batch.
